pages.text: A fluid of conductivity σ crossing a field B at speed u sees an electric field uB. The load takes a fraction k of it; the current density j = σuB(1 − k) flows to the electrodes, and the power per volume is p = σu²B²k(1 − k).
$(thing)Set$(): Magnetic field B, Flow speed u, Load factor k.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Magnet supply ripple: the field varies by ±1%·d.

$(thing)Limits$(): Electrode arcing: current density above 100 A/cm²; The pumps cannot drive the flow that fast; The channel is overheating.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Power output follows the electric power.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Effective field: B·(1 + 0.01·d)$(br)Current density: j = σuB(1 − k)$(br)Power density: p = σu²B²k(1 − k)$(br)Electric power: P = p·V$(br)Dynamic pressure: q = ½ρu²
